newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH Q1 C/A GAP MORE THAN $1.5 BLN-C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: POLISH Q1 C/A GAP MORE THAN $1.5 BLN-C.BANK.

text.p: Polish current account gap after the first quarter of this year exceeded $1.5 billion while the trade gap was more than $3 billion, Rzeczpospolita daily quoted deputy central bank president as saying.
Witold Kozinski said Polish exports did not need any further stimulation because they were growing at a satisfactory rate but the fast growth of imports was a problem.
The National Bank of Poland will release precise current account data for March in early May.
The current account gap was at $1.13 billion in February while trade gap was $2.18 billion.

Kozinski said Poland's trade gap might reach five percent of gross domestic product this year against one percent in 1996, but he added such a deficit would not be a problem unless its growth rate continues.
The finance ministry expects the gap at 3-3.5 percent this year.
